items.b: GEMFIELDS SELLS ALL 44 COMMERCIAL EMERALD LOTS FOR $29.6 MILLION AT $9.72 A CARAT
items.t: Gemfields' commercial-quality rough emerald auction, held 24 August to 10 September 2026 and viewed in Jaipur, took total revenues of USD 29.6 million with all 44 lots offered sold, a 100% clearance by number and by weight. The average realised price of USD 9.72 a carat is 30.3% above the USD 7.46 of the November-December 2025 commercial sale and 118.4% above the USD 4.45 of March 2024, and the average has risen at each of the last four commercial auctions. Carats sold fell 10.5% to 3,047,650. Sixty-three companies placed bids, against 55 last time. Proceeds are repatriated in full to Kagem in Zambia, 75% owned by Gemfields and 25% by the Industrial Development Corporation of Zambia.

items.b: SILVER SHEDS $2.19 TO $63.94 SINCE THE 9 SEPTEMBER MARK; ALL FOUR METALS LOWER
items.t: On Kitco's bid at 06:01 ET, silver is $63.94 against $66.13 on 9 September, palladium $1,290.00 against $1,335.00, platinum $1,797.00 against $1,841.00 and gold $4,347.30 against $4,389.30, falls of 3.312%, 3.371%, 2.390% and 0.957%. No mark was filed for 10 September, so each change spans two sessions. Kitco's own session change prints all four metals higher on the Friday, from its prior close; the two reference points are different and both are carried. The gold-silver ratio widened to 68.0 from 66.4.

items.b: BULGARI 9.86-CARAT KASHMIR SAPPHIRE RING CARRIES HKD 9.5M HIGH ESTIMATE AT PHILLIPS HONG KONG
items.t: Phillips offers 95 lots at its Hong Kong Jewels Auction on 29 September, led by a Bulgari ring centring a cushion-shaped 9.86-carat Kashmir sapphire between two shield-shaped diamonds, reported at a high estimate of HKD 9.5 million, about USD 1.2 million. That works out to HKD 963,500 a carat. Coloured stones take seven of the ten highest estimates; a 13.82-carat Burmese sapphire is estimated at HKD 2 million to HKD 3 million, HKD 217,100 a carat, so the smaller Kashmir stone is valued at 4.4 times the larger Burmese per carat. Estimates as reported by Rapaport, 8 September, from the Phillips website.

items.b: URWERK PUTS THE UR-150 IN 18-CARAT GOLD AT $140,000, LIMITED TO 25 PIECES
items.t: The UR-150 Golden Scorpion, shown at Geneva Watch Days, has a 2N yellow gold case middle with concentric grooves over a sandblasted Grade 5 titanium back, and is limited to 25 pieces at $140,000 each in the United States per JCK. The Swiss list is CHF 105,000 excluding taxes, 19.3% above the CHF 88,000 of the 2024 titanium Titan, which ran to 50 pieces per variant. The two published prices sit on different currencies and tax bases and neither source gives a rate, so both are carried as they stand.

items.b: KAY CUTS ITS ASSORTMENT ABOUT 20% AND ADDS MEN'S SHOPS IN ABOUT 200 STORES
items.t: Signet's largest banner has reduced its assortment by about 20% over the past year in every category, under a brand platform called Love All In that is live on the website, in advertising and on social from this week. Men's shops of about 25 linear feet go into roughly 200 of Kay's 1,003 locations, which comprise 882 stores and 121 outlets, or 39.6% of the 2,534 Signet had open at 1 August. Store redesign and packaging follow in 2027, and an open-sell pilot takes Rocksbox pieces out from under glass. Kay president Julie Yoakum is the named source in both WWD and JCK.
